# phasetwo_gateway_app (Resource)

A website behind Keycloak login with [Gateway](https://phasetwo.io/docs/self-service/gateway/): users of the realm sign in before they reach it, and the website itself does not change.

Creating an app creates its OIDC client in the realm, generates the origin secret and requests the public hostname's certificate. It does **not** serve traffic. To go live:

1. Make your origin refuse requests that lack `origin_secret` in the `X-Phasetwo-Origin-Secret` header.
2. Point `public_hostname` at `dns_target` with a CNAME.
3. Add a [`phasetwo_gateway_app_activation`](gateway_app_activation), which verifies the origin and starts serving.

~> **`origin_secret` is stored in Terraform state.** The API returns it once, on create, and Terraform is the only place left to keep it. Treat the state as secret. An imported app has no `origin_secret`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phasetwo_gateway_app" "admin" {
  realm_id        = phasetwo_realm.customer.id
  name            = "Internal admin console"
  public_hostname = "admin.example.com"
  origin_url      = "https://admin-origin.example.com"
  health_path     = "/healthz"

  # Anyone who can sign in may read /reports; only staff reach /admin; every other path is
  # refused. Every rule that matches a request must pass, so a rule on "/" would apply to all.
  policy = {
    default = "deny"
    rules = [
      { path_prefix = "/reports", methods = ["GET"] },
      { path_prefix = "/admin", groups_any = ["/staff"] },
    ]
  }

  header_mappings = {
    "X-Phasetwo-Auth-Email"  = "email"
    "X-Phasetwo-Auth-Groups" = "groups"
  }
  assertion_enabled = true
}

# Users go to the Gateway: point the public hostname at it.
resource "aws_route53_record" "admin" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = phasetwo_gateway_app.admin.public_hostname
  type    = "CNAME"
  records = [phasetwo_gateway_app.admin.dns_target]
  ttl     = 300
}

# Hand the origin secret to whatever runs the origin, here as a secret its ingress reads.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "origin_secret" {
  secret_id     = var.origin_secret_id
  secret_string = phasetwo_gateway_app.admin.origin_secret
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.
- `origin_url` (String) Where the website runs, e.g. `https://admin-origin.example.com`: HTTPS with a valid certificate, port 443 or 8443, a different hostname from `public_hostname`, an optional base path and no trailing slash. Cannot change while the app is active; remove its `phasetwo_gateway_app_activation` first.
- `public_hostname` (String) Hostname users visit, e.g. `admin.example.com`, in lower case. Changing it replaces the app, which creates a new origin secret.
- `realm_id` (String) ID of the realm (deployment) whose users sign in.

### Optional

- `assertion_claims` (List of String) Claims in the assertion besides `sub`. Defaults to `["email", "preferred_username"]`.
- `assertion_enabled` (Boolean) Send a signed JWT in `X-Phasetwo-Auth-Assertion` on every request, valid for 60 seconds, so the origin can verify who the user is against `jwks_url`.
- `header_mappings` (Map of String) Headers to send to the origin on every request, from header name (`X-Phasetwo-Auth-*`) to claim: `sub`, `email`, `email_verified`, `preferred_username`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `groups`, `realm_roles` or `client_roles`. The Gateway removes any header with these names that a browser sends. Trust them only at an origin that requires the origin secret.
- `health_path` (String) A path on the origin that returns 2xx when the secret is present and has no side effects. Verification sends four requests to it. Defaults to `/`.
- `idle_timeout_seconds` (Number) Sign the user out after this long without a request. 60 to 86400; defaults to 1800.
- `max_session_seconds` (Number) Sign the user out this long after they signed in. 300 to 604800; defaults to 28800.
- `policy` (Attributes) Who may reach which paths. Without it, any user who can sign in to the realm reaches every path. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policy))
- `post_logout_redirect_uri` (String) HTTPS URL to send users to after they sign out at `/_p2/logout`. Without it they see a Phase Two page.

### Read-Only

- `assertion_issuer` (String) `iss` of identity assertions.
- `callback_url` (String) Redirect URI registered on the client.
- `client_id` (String) The OIDC client created in the realm, `gateway-<public_hostname>`. Client roles for `client_roles_any` are defined on it.
- `dns_target` (String) Create a CNAME from `public_hostname` to this.
- `id` (String) App ID. Also the `aud` of the identity assertions the Gateway sends to the origin.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer of the realm.
- `jwks_url` (String) Public keys that verify identity assertions.
- `origin_secret` (String, Sensitive) The value your origin must require in `origin_secret_header`. Only known for an app this configuration created.
- `origin_secret_header` (String) Header that carries the origin secret: `X-Phasetwo-Origin-Secret`.
- `status` (String) `PENDING` until first activated, `ACTIVE` while serving, `DISABLED` after deactivation.

<a id="nestedatt--policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policy`

Optional:

- `default` (String) `authenticated` (any signed-in user, the default) or `deny` (only paths a rule matches).
- `rules` (Attributes List) Every rule whose `path_prefix` and `methods` match a request applies, and all of them must pass; `deny` wins. Within a rule each list is "any of", and the lists combine with AND. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policy--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--policy--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policy.rules`

Required:

- `path_prefix` (String) Path prefix, e.g. `/admin`. Matches whole path segments, case-insensitively: `/admin` matches `/Admin/users` but not `/administrator`.

Optional:

- `claims_equal` (Map of String) Claims that must equal these values, e.g. `{ email_verified = "true" }`. Keys are the claims `header_mappings` allows.
- `client_roles_any` (List of String) The user holds at least one of these roles on the app's client (`client_id`).
- `effect` (String) `require` (the default): the conditions must hold. `deny`: always refuse.
- `groups_any` (List of String) The user is in at least one of these groups, by full path, e.g. `/staff/support`.
- `methods` (List of String) Upper-case HTTP methods the rule applies to; every method when omitted. `GET` covers `HEAD`.
- `realm_roles_any` (List of String) The user holds at least one of these realm roles.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <realm_id>/<app_id>. The origin secret cannot be recovered by import.
terraform import phasetwo_gateway_app.admin 3f9a1c2e-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/8b0d4e6f-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
